key_insight: A single transformer-based Riemannian flow matching model can learn Standard Model event structure directly from LHC data across sub-GeV to TeV scales using only on-shell physics priors.
engineering_relevance: This suggests data-driven generative models can replace or augment Monte Carlo simulation for high-energy physics event generation while preserving physically valid kinematics.
method: Train ShellFlow on ~10^9 ATLAS Open Data pp collision events.
Condition on recorded event composition and generate each particle on its on-shell manifold.
Use only two priors: the on-shell condition and the invariant-mass formula.
evidence_signal: From a single training run, the model reproduces intra-particle kinematics, J/5, , and Z resonances at PDG positions, the leptonic Weinberg angle, W/top masses, and inter-particle correlations not included in the training objective.
watch_item: Performance depends on large-scale labeled collision data and careful enforcement of physical constraints, so generalization beyond the ATLAS domain or to rare processes still needs validation.
paper_title: Learning Standard Model structure from LHC data with Riemannian flow matching
